claim: *Commodity intelligence in a governed engineering environment.* General capabilities from a foundation model become useful engineering machinery when connected to an agentic harness and a governed engineering environment. The environment contains both the existing system and the engineering structure used to guide and govern work. Engineers develop and maintain this environment.
topology: The trained foundation model feeds the model inside the engineering system. Outputs/context connect the model and harness; actions/tool-results-or-evidence connect harness and GEE. Guidance originates at GEE, runs below the columns, and enters the foundation model. Governance originates at GEE, follows a separate top route, and terminates at a boundary marker crossing the Actions shaft. The sole engineer arrow enters GEE. No engineer-to-model, engineer-to-harness or training/fine-tuning route remains.

Component and enclosure headings are bold 9.5–10 pt. Model properties and guidance/governance relation names are bold 9 pt. Explanatory subtitles are italic 9 pt; implications, facilities, examples and exchange labels are regular 9 pt.
redesign: Author corrections to the compact review draft distinguish the foundation model, harness facilities, project-specific GEE structure, and the sources and targets of guidance and governance. The engineer only develops and maintains the GEE. The northern trained model feeds the foundation model inside the agentic engineering system.
alt: Model development transforms training data through training into a trained foundation model, which supplies the foundation model within the agentic engineering system. The foundation model exchanges outputs and context with an agentic harness; the harness exchanges actions and tool results or evidence with the governed engineering environment. Four model properties have engineering implications: broad reasoning enables delegated implementation; probabilistic output requires independent assurance; finite working state motivates external representations and retrieval; inexpensive inference enables repeated exploration and revision. Harness facilities are tools and integrations, context management, interposition or hooks, and parallel or staged execution. The GEE contains the existing system and engineering structure. Guidance originates in the GEE and supplies knowledge to influence reasoning; governance originates in the GEE and constrains actions and controls acceptance. The engineer develops and maintains the GEE.
